item.title: 504 Fijians receive free medical care on Indonesian Navy hospital ship
item.description: An Indonesian Navy hospital vessel, KRI dr Wahidin Sudirohusodo-991, has provided free medical services to 504 patients in Suva over two days, bringing essential healthcare services closer to members of the public. The crew was farewelled last night, with Minister for Immigration Viliame Naupoto thanking the Indonesian Government and its naval crew for their service to the people of Fiji. Speaking
item.content:encoded:
An Indonesian Navy hospital vessel, KRI dr Wahidin Sudirohusodo-991, has provided free medical services to 504 patients in Suva over two days, bringing essential healthcare services closer to members of the public.

The crew was farewelled last night, with Minister for Immigration Viliame Naupoto thanking the Indonesian Government and its naval crew for their service to the people of Fiji. Speaking at a farewell reception, Naupoto said the visit was particularly meaningful as Fiji celebrated its Independence Day, adding that the medical services had given many Fijians renewed hope and access to essential healthcare. He said there could be no more fitting gift to the people of Fiji than improved health and well-being. The ship provided eye checks, dental care, radiology and electrocardiogram (ECG) screenings in collaboration with the Ministry of Health. Naupoto acknowledged the ship’s 316 crew members, including naval personnel, doctors, nurses, media officers and university students, for their contribution during the visit. He said the visit had also created valuable opportunities for Fijian healthcare workers to exchange knowledge and learn from their Indonesian counterparts. The visit was part of Indonesia’s 2026 Navy Hospital Ship Port Visit programme, carried out under the theme Bridging Nations, Serving Humanity. Naupoto said the initiative reflected Indonesia’s continued support for Fiji and its commitment to strengthening healthcare cooperation across the Pacific. He also thanked the Indonesian Government and the Indonesian Embassy in Suva for coordinating the visit. The ship is scheduled to depart Fiji today for the Solomon Islands and Papua New Guinea, where it will continue its humanitarian activities. Naupoto wished the crew a safe journey and expressed hope that they would return to Fiji in the future.

item.title: Parliament could sit until Christmas Eve to complete Constitution Bill process - Rabuka
item.description: Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka highlighted this after the Joint Parliamentary Select Committee on Constitution Review met at Parliament today. Rabuka says Parliament was originally expected to hold its final sitting in the first week of November, but this could now be extended.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka highlighted this after the Joint Parliamentary Select Committee on Constitution Review met at Parliament today.

Rabuka says Parliament was originally expected to hold its final sitting in the first week of November, but this could now be extended.

He says Parliament may return in the first week of November to seek additional sitting days, with further sittings possibly held in the second or third week of the month.

Insert: PM on the Constitution Ammendment Bill. 12th October,26

The Prime Minister says the previous parliamentary sitting allowed 30 days for the process, but the past week was spent dealing with other matters.

He says today's committee meeting was the first opportunity to finalise the agenda and programme for the week.

When asked whether other political parties had raised concerns during the meeting, Rabuka says no further concerns were raised about the main issues in the proposed constitutional changes.

He also says Cabinet has agreed with the Special Committee on the Constitution.

The Constitution Amendment Bill has already passed its second reading and will need another vote in Parliament before it can proceed to a national referendum.

item.title: Diabetes Fiji calls for free insulin syringes for children with Type 1 diabetes
item.description: Diabetes Fiji is calling on the Government to provide insulin syringes as part of the treatment package for insulin-dependent patients, particularly children and other vulnerable people who struggle to afford the essential medical supplies. In its Fiji Day message, Diabetes Fiji Executive Director Marawa Kini says while the Government provides insulin through the public health system, families con
item.content:encoded:
Diabetes Fiji is calling on the Government to provide insulin syringes as part of the treatment package for insulin-dependent patients, particularly children and other vulnerable people who struggle to afford the essential medical supplies.

In its Fiji Day message, Diabetes Fiji Executive Director Marawa Kini says while the Government provides insulin through the public health system, families continue to face the financial burden of purchasing syringes needed to administer the life-saving medication.

Kini says access to insulin is incomplete without consistent access to the devices required to administer it.

He says parents caring for children with Type 1 diabetes should not have to worry about whether they can afford the syringes their children need every day.

Diabetes Fiji says it currently supports 98 active members through its Young Diabetes Fiji Programme across the Central, Western and Northern divisions.

The organisation says previous programme records between 2020 and 2023 included approximately 500 children and young people, from infancy through to young adulthood.

Kini says Fiji must demonstrate the same urgency in addressing the needs of people living with diabetes as it does in responding to other national health challenges.

He stresses that the call is not intended to undermine support for people living with HIV or those affected by drug dependence, but to ensure all vulnerable populations receive equitable access to healthcare.

He says every person deserves care, compassion and access to appropriate treatment, regardless of their condition or financial circumstances.

Diabetes Fiji is also calling for a structured national review of diabetes treatment, including access to insulin pens, continuous glucose monitoring systems and insulin pumps, as well as newer medicines for Type 2 diabetes.

The organisation says the review should involve the Ministry of Health and Medical Services, clinicians, pharmacists, people living with diabetes, academic institutions and development partners.

It says the review should assess what is clinically appropriate, affordable and sustainable for Fiji, with particular attention to children, rural and maritime communities, and economically disadvantaged families.

Kini says modernising diabetes care is about preventing complications such as blindness, kidney disease, heart disease and amputations, while improving the quality of life of people living with the condition.

He is also urging corporate Fiji, donors and development partners to invest in diabetes care through funding for medical supplies, screening programmes, technology, education and patient support services.

Diabetes Fiji says it is ready to work with the Government and other partners to improve access to treatment and ensure people living with diabetes are not left behind.

Kini says Fiji Day should serve as a reminder that national unity must also be reflected in how the country cares for its most vulnerable people.

He says no child should have to face a lifelong condition without access to the essential tools needed to manage it.
